intent: Hold the open state of one modal dialog and tie its trigger to the centered popup that blocks the rest of the page while open.
typical_uses: A short form or decision the user completes before returning to the page
A detail view that needs the user's full attention

dont_use_when.situation: A confirmation the user must answer explicitly, which must not close on a press outside it
A panel that slides in from an edge of the screen
An edge panel the user can dismiss with a swipe gesture
A floating panel anchored to its trigger that leaves the page interactive
A brief status message that needs no answer

invariants.text: `open` and `defaultOpen` are both accepted; `defaultOpen` seeds the initial state and is ignored afterwards, and when `open` is given it wins and the component follows it on every render.

With `modal` at its default `true`, focus is trapped in the popup, page scroll is locked and presses outside the popup reach nothing on the page; `'trap-focus'` traps focus without locking scroll or adding the primitive's own blocking layer; DialogContent's visible backdrop still covers the page unless `showBackdrop={false}`; `false` leaves the page interactive.

Escape and a press outside the popup close the dialog, reporting the reason to `onOpenChange`; with nested dialogs open, only the topmost one closes. `disablePointerDismissal` keeps an outside press from closing it, and for a non-modal dialog also keeps focus moving out from closing it.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Update the state `open` reads from inside `onOpenChange`

children.states: children is the root's content, either React nodes or a function of the active trigger's payload that returns them
children.because: `React.ReactNode | PayloadChildRenderFunction<Payload>` - the function form receives `{ payload }` from whichever trigger opened the dialog. The compiler emits one JSON type per property, and a function has no JSON Schema representation.

onOpenChange.states: onOpenChange is a callback called with the next open state and event details, not a value
onOpenChange.because: `(open: boolean, eventDetails) => void`; the second argument carries Base UI's change-event details, including the reason (a trigger press, an outside press, Escape, a close press, focus moving out or an imperative action). No JSON Schema type covers a function.

onOpenChangeComplete.states: onOpenChangeComplete is a callback called with the open state once the open or close animation has finished
onOpenChangeComplete.because: `(open: boolean) => void` - a function, which no JSON Schema type covers.

actionsRef.states: actionsRef is a ref the root fills with imperative `close` and `unmount` actions
actionsRef.because: `React.RefObject<DialogRootActions | null>` - a ref object holding functions, which no JSON Schema type covers.

handle.states: handle is an opaque object from the primitive's Dialog.createHandle(), shared with a trigger placed outside this root
handle.because: `DialogHandle<Payload>` is a class instance holding the dialog's store, not data; the kit re-exports no createHandle, so a caller imports it from the primitive.

modal.states: modal is true, false or the string 'trap-focus'
modal.because: `boolean | 'trap-focus'` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a boolean-or-string union is left unasserted.

triggerId.states: triggerId is the id of the trigger a controlled dialog is open for, or null
triggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

defaultTriggerId.states: defaultTriggerId is the id of the trigger an initially open dialog is open for, or null
defaultTriggerId.because: `string | null` - the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so a string-or-null union is left unasserted.

good.title: A short task with a composed cancel action
good.code:
<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Rename</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Rename project</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>The new name is visible to everyone on the team.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Cancel</DialogClose>
      <Button onClick={handleRename}>Save</Button>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>

bad.title: A controlled dialog nothing can close
bad.why: Without `onOpenChange` nothing turns `open` false, so Escape, an outside press and the built-in close button all leave the dialog on screen.
